title: Core Resolution
text: PCs are assumed to be competent in their own right, based on their Background and Archetype. Only roll if there's a genuine risk of failure involved. If a character could do something and has the time and resources to do it, let them do it — no roll needed. The core resolution system is (2d10 + stat) vs Target. Target starts at 12, but can be adjusted per the NPC's own target number, or the scene's target number. This represents the general level of risk a whole moment carries, or an NPC represents, or an aspect of either. That's every check in this system — attacks, saves, skill use, all of it. What a stat actually represents. Every check happens because something's genuinely at stake, and the stat you roll is the part of your character being tested in that moment — acting on the world, or holding up against something acting on you. title: Guard Stat
text: Every character has a damage buffer called Guard (full explanation on Combat ). It's not chosen — it's calculated automatically: your highest-bonus stat, excluding your cast stat (and Wandslinger stat, if taken) and the governing stat of every weapon currently equipped in a hand slot. CON is never a cast or weapon stat, so it's always eligible. Guard Stat (if it lands there) Concept STR — Brute Force Physically blocks and overpowers incoming attacks (only possible if STR isn't your weapon or cast stat) DEX — Reflexes Dodges and weaves; full hits become glancing ones (only possible if DEX isn't your weapon or cast stat) CON — Endurance Classic tank: physically tough, shrugs off blows INT — Tactics Reads the fight, positions so blows land where they hurt least WIS — Awareness Danger sense; flinches away before the worst lands CHA — Presence Force of personality throws off an attacker's aim

title: What's in This Document — Archetypes
text: Three chassis — Wayfarer ( Grit , martial maneuvers), Agent ( Leverage , Contingency , Skills), Syberist (real spellcasting, four traditions including Artificer). Example: a Wayfarer spends 2 Grit on Shield to impose Disadvantage on every attack against an ally this round. Full page →

title: What's in This Document — Magic
text: Possession-based casting (you need enough shards on hand, not a daily spell-slot budget), six potency tiers from free Cantrips to world-altering Mythic effects, and the Overcast Backlash Pool for attempting a cast you can't quite afford. Example: a Minor-tier attack spell deals 1d6 + your cast stat, identical in shape to a Medium weapon — magic and steel compete on the same terms. Full page →

title: What's in This Document — Combat
text: Guard -and- Wound HP model, zone -based positioning, weapon tiers, and the full Wayfarer Grit Maneuvers list. Example: a Wound reduces your max Guard by 2, and current Guard refills to that new, lower max — you're worse off going forward, not just hurt right now. Full page →

title: What's in This Document — Exploration
text: Reaction checks for NPC disposition, and a d6-based random event roll for travel and dungeon exploration. Example: rolling a 1 on the Travel Event table means a Mishap — a full extra day added to the journey. Full page →

title: What's in This Document — Enemy Design
text: Build any monster from a handful of numbers ( Base Target , Guard, weapon tier, damage bonus) instead of a full stat block. Example: a Mook has no Wound slot at all — Guard alone decides when it's down. Full page →

text: How PCs grow — XP via themed question packages, leveling, and the Vertical (universal stat/Guard growth) and Lateral (archetype-specific options) tracks. title: Stat Bonus Generation
text: Roll 3d6 per stat (summed), look up the bonus. Changed from 2d6 specifically to make the extremes rarer and narrow the total spread — 3d6 keeps a genuine bell curve with more room in the tails to tune how rare ±2 actually is. 3d6 (sum) Bonus Success vs 12 3–6 −2 28% 7–9 −1 36% 10–11 0 45% 12–14 +1 55% 15–18 +2 64% No stat can ever exceed +3, under any circumstance. A maxed 3d6 roll alone caps at +2; stacking a same-stat Background bonus on a maxed roll can already reach +3 at creation. Vertical growth (see Advancement) can also reach +3 for a stat that didn't max out this way — but once any stat hits +3, it's simply not a legal target for further Vertical picks; the player points those at a different stat instead. Mercy adjustment: if no stat is positive after rolling, raise two stats to +1 each, or one stat to +2 (player's choice). Applies to the raw roll, before Background bonuses stac

title: Choice Guidance
text: What makes each step's decision strong or weak — tested against real builds, not abstract advice.

title: Choice Guidance — Background
text: Pick one whose stat bonus lands on the stat your archetype actually wants. A mismatched Background isn't illegal, just a real, felt inefficiency unless the concept specifically calls for it.

title: Choice Guidance — Archetype
text: Wayfarer = frontline durability, Agent = breadth and narrative leverage, Syberist = real spellcasting (including Artificer, the crafting-flavored tradition). If torn, ask which resource ( Grit / Leverage / shards) sounds more fun to spend during play. If Wayfarer or Agent, decide Wandslinger here too — it sets a cast stat immediately, which matters for Guard Stat later.

title: Choice Guidance — Rolling & the Mercy Rule
text: If mercy fires, raising one stat to +2 concentrates power; raising two to +1 spreads it. The mercy check applies to the raw roll , before any Background bonus stacks on top.

title: Choice Guidance — Weapon & Armor
text: Decide melee-or-ranged first, then which stat governs it — DEX doesn't automatically mean ranged. Check the relevant stat against Weapon Proficiency before committing narratively to a concept; if it fails, fall back to the highest tier you qualify for, or go ranged instead. Worth remembering here: whatever you pick directly decides your Guard Stat pool, calculated next.

title: Choice Guidance — Guard Stat
text: No longer a choice — it's automatically your highest-bonus stat, excluding your cast stat and whatever your equipped weapon(s) use. A Heavy weapon on your best physical stat locks that stat out of Guard, so a genuinely tanky build often wants its offensive stat and its naturally-high stat to be different from the start.

title: Choice Guidance — Languages
text: A high-INT build should pick languages that actually matter for the campaign. A −2-or-lower INT build's illiteracy is a real constraint worth embracing, not working around — it's supposed to bite.

title: Choice Guidance — Starting Wealth
text: A caster should convert a meaningful chunk of the 200gp into refined shards — 100–150gp is reasonable. A pure martial build can spend close to zero on shards and put everything into gear instead. Safety Valve If a player is unhappy with the whole character — not a single bad roll the mercy rule already covers, but the build overall not feeling right — player and GM can agree to start over completely. title: Talents & Expertise
text: Talents grant Advantage on relevant checks — the universal expertise system every archetype has access to, tied to Background rather than class. Every Background below grants two. A GM may rule a check succeeds automatically if a character is also carrying relevant equipment (the Healing Talent plus a Healing Toolkit to treat a Wound ).

title: Languages
text: Common is free to everyone. INT bonus ≤ −2 means illiterate — speaks known languages but can't read or write any. INT bonus 0 grants +1 extra language per point. Non-human Backgrounds grant their ancestral language free , separate from the INT-based count — noted per Background below where it applies.

title: Dragonmarked Houses
text: Two distinct kinds of House-lineage Background exist for each House: Agent (works for the House, no Mark) and Marked (carries the House's Least Mark). Most people connected to a House, even by blood, never manifest a mark — Agent Backgrounds are the common case. Only a Background specifically named "[House] Marked" grants one; a career-tied Agent Background never does. Free — no shard cost, narrow and reliable. Being Marked carries real House Duty, true for every Marked Background: the House can call on you for tasks you can't easily refuse, and Excoriation — being cast out, marked but disowned — is a genuine, heavy consequence for defying them seriously, not a minor setback. Less personal freedom, offset by real power. text: Distinct from a career-tied House Background — most people in a marked family never manifest a Dragonmark. This is specifically someone the mark chose. title: Wayfarer
text: Fighter/Barbarian chassis — Grit resource, a Guard bonus of +2, and a full martial toolkit through Grit Maneuvers. Grit starts at 2, +1 at even levels. +1 Grit per Turn of rest, if not Deprived, up to your max. A full pool (6 at most, by level 8) is reachable within an hour of rest — unlike Wounds, which Turns of rest don't touch at all.

title: Wayfarer — Grit Maneuvers
text: All maneuvers are available from level 1 — gated by Grit cost, not character level. The stronger ones just cost more Grit. One Maneuver per action, no stacking. Each Maneuver either is your action for the turn (Guard Stance, Taunt, Rally, Read the Fight) or modifies your one attack (Focus, Cleave, Guarded Strike). Since a turn only grants one attack, only one attack-modifying Maneuver can ever apply to a single attack — Focus and Cleave can't both land on the same swing. Maneuvers combine across different PCs' turns, or across different rounds for the same PC, never by stacking two modifiers onto one action. title: Agent — Leverage & Contingency
text: Leverage starts at 2, +1 per level. Regenerates during downtime, once per lull in the action — not from resting a Turn , and deliberately not locked to any one setting. The player describes how they're using the downtime to prepare; the GM decides which mental stat (CHA/WIS/INT) actually fits that description, then rolls 2d10 + that stat vs Target 12. Success regenerates 1 Leverage. The GM may shift the Target based on how favorable the environment is — a barren cave with WIS chosen might push the Target up; Sharn with CHA chosen might pull it down. Can be spent on an ally's behalf, not just your own declarations. Contingency is what Leverage buys: retroactively "already having prepared" for a specific moment. title: Agent — Agent Flavors
text: Three concept archetypes on the same chassis, differing only in what kind of Contingency each leans into and what regenerates Leverage. Rogue / "Cutthroat" — physical, logistical Contingencies. Leverage regenerates by casing a location before the job. Pairs with Exploit the Opening/Take Aim and Many Pockets. Diplomat / "Emissary" — relational, informational Contingencies. title: Artificer, in Detail
text: Started as its own fourth archetype (Cannith-Touched), rebuilt into a Syberist tradition after three separate problems traced back to the same root cause: the whole Infusion subsystem was 5e's Artificer mechanic imported wholesale into a document otherwise built on OSR conventions. Every fix attempted was patching around that mismatch rather than fixing it. Matches Wildspoken's own precedent — a Druid didn't need to be its own archetype either. title: Magic Baseline
text: Possession, not consumption. Casting means possessing enough shards to pay a tier's cost, not consuming a fixed daily resource. Cantrip tier requires only possessing ≥1 shard as a focus, never spent — real mechanical effects (Spark and above) require actual casting access, not just carrying shards. Shards are two separate economic goods, not one. Raw shards (dust) — loose, unrefined, 5cp each — power Cantrip and Spark. Refined shards — cut and processed, 10gp each — power Minor and above. A Wandslinger's entire build only ever touches raw dust; they never pay refined-shard prices, since they're hard-capped below Minor. title: Magic Baseline — Overcasting
text: Only applies to Minor, Moderate, Major, and Mythic — the refined-shard economy. There is no overcasting Cantrip or Spark. Those two run on raw shards (dust) with a flat, known cost — nothing to fall short of, since the cost is never uncertain. A character who can't afford Spark's flat cost simply can't cast it. A caster can always attempt a cast even without enough shards to pay for it — but the spell only actually manifests on a genuinely good roll. Resolved entirely with a d6 pool, nothing to calculate. Pool size by tier: Minor 4d6, Moderate 3d6, Major 2d6, Mythic 1d6. More than half the cost missing? Remove one die. No floor — the pool can hit 0. Pool at 0: instant death, no roll. The only way to fail this hard — only reachable attempting Mythic tier with less than half the cost on hand. Add rerolls equal to CON bonus — reroll that many lowest dice once each, keep the better result. C

title: Magic Baseline — Spell Resolution: Attack vs. Effect
text: Attack spells — aimed at a target, competes with a weapon's role. Caster rolls to-hit like a weapon, plus shards cost. Effect spells — everything else (wards, buffs, heals, utility). No caster roll. Willing target: works automatically. Unwilling target: target rolls a resistance check. Worked Example — Attack vs. Effect Attack spell: Ilyara (Shardbound Syberist, INT +2) casts a Minor-tier bolt at a Standard-tier bandit. title: Core Resolution
text: Full mechanic and design philosophy on Foundations ; stat generation and the Mercy rule live on Character Creation , since that's genuinely where rolling stats happens. Quick reference: roll 2d10 + stat bonus, succeed on 12 or higher. Advantage /Disadvantage: roll 3d10, keep the best or worst two. Critical Hit (doubles on the counted dice = max damage) and Damage Floor (minimum 1 damage on any hit) are also covered there — same rule for weapon attacks and Attack spells alike; Disadvantage never crits, no exceptions.

title: Economy
text: Raw shards: 5cp each (= 1 arrow), power Cantrip/Spark. Refined shards: 10gp each, power Minor+ and permanent magic items. Starting wealth: 200gp, flexible — spend on refined shards, gear, or both.

title: Status Effects
text: Four named, temporary states appear throughout this document. Stated once here, referenced by name everywhere else. Status Effect Clears when Reeling Disadvantage on your next roll That roll happens, or an ally clears it early (Rally Cry, Combat Mending Moderate+) Rattled Disadvantage on your next two rolls Both rolls happen, or an ally clears it early (same sources as Reeling ) Deprived Disadvantage on all checks; no Guard recovery from resting a Turn Eating, drinking, and a full day's rest Surprised Skip your action entirely for Round 1 Automatically, after Round 1 ends No stacking, universally — a second source of Reeling or Rattled while one is already pending never extends it; whichever is already active resolves first.

title: Guard & Wounds
text: Guard = 4 + Guard Stat bonus + archetype bonus + armor + shield, floor 1. Restores fully after a Turn of rest. 1 Wound slot at creation, second at level 4, third at level 8. An open Wound reduces max Guard by 2; current Guard refills to the new max , floor 1. The next roll is made with Disadvantage (" Reeling "), plus a Wound Complication (d6). Wounds don't heal from resting a Turn and can't close mid-combat.

text: Combat Mending (in combat, costs an action + shards per tier): restores Guard , up to current max — Minor 1d8+stat, Moderate 2d8+stat, Major 2d8+stat, Mythic 4d8+stat, same dice as damage at each tier. title: Zones & Range
text: Melee, Near, and Far are the GM's framework for adjudicating positioning within a real, shared scene. The scene comes first — the tavern, the rafters, the street outside — tracked collectively at the table like any theater-of-the-mind moment. What "Far" represents flexes with the scene: a hundred yards on an open field, or just "through the door" in a cramped tavern. Each character reads Melee/Near/Far relative to themselves. Two people can both be Far from a melee cluster while being nowhere near each other. A character with a bow reads more of a room as Near than a melee-only character standing in the same spot, since their reach extends further. Real-world logic governs each reading; the framework keeps that logic consistent at the table. Disengaging tracks the shared fiction. A melee-capable hostile close enough, in the group's shared imagination, to threaten you triggers a Disengage

title: Initiative
text: 2d10 + DEX + weapon modifier − armor penalty − shield penalty, once per fight, fixed order. Weapon tier Modifier Light +3 Medium +1 Heavy −1 Massive (monster-scale) −3 Armor / Shield Penalty Light armor — Medium armor −1 Heavy armor −2 Shield −1 Tower Shield −3 Ties: higher DEX bonus goes first; a quick reroll between tied parties only if that's also equal. Every other source that touches Initiative, consolidated here rather than scattered: Reeling Hard (a Wound Complication result) overrides the roll entirely — Initiative order drops to last for the rest of the fight, not a numeric penalty stacked on the formula above. Not on my watch! (a Basic Grit Maneuver, 1 Grit) lets a Wayfarer reroll their own Initiative roll once, keeping the better result. Nothing else in this document currently touches Initiative.

title: Surprise & Ambushes
text: Each character rolls 2d10+WIS individually. First success can warn others ( Advantage for anyone yet to roll). Failure means skipping the Round 1 action only.

title: Morale
text: Roll 2d10 vs Target 12 to hold. Target drops to 10 while a named leader is present and alive — losing the leader raises it back to 12 immediately. Checks fire once each at: first casualty, 50% losses, leader down (checked at Target 12, the bonus already gone). Ported from OSE's 2d6-roll-under Morale; Target 12 is the default for an average group, not fixed — see Scenario Target Modifiers for deviating from it by enemy type. title: Item Slots
text: Ten item slots total: 2 hand, 2 body, 6 backpack. Hand slots hold what's actively wielded; body slots hold worn gear for easy access in combat; backpack slots hold everything else. Using something already in hand costs your normal action for the turn — attacking, drinking a held potion, activating a held gadget, all the same, no different from anything else you might do with your action. Producing or stowing an item is also a full action, not an add-on — drawing a new weapon, swapping what's in a hand slot, retrieving something from a body slot, or from a backpack slot (Many Pockets removes the cost for backpack retrieval specifically). Since a turn only has one action, producing something and using it both happen in the same turn only if it was already in hand; otherwise it's draw this turn, use it next. title: Toolkits & Usage
text: Every item — weapons, armor, toolkits, torches, rations — has three usage dots. When all three are filled, it's depleted or destroyed. What fills a dot differs by item type, but the shared shape means only one rule to learn: Item type Usage dot trigger Weapons/Armor/Ammo Roll a d6 after combat for each item used; on a 1–3, mark a dot Torches/Light sources Mark a dot whenever a relevant exploration roll calls for it Rations Mark a dot when taking a long rest without first taking the time to hunt or forage Toolkits Mark a dot every time it's actually used for its purpose Everything else GM's call Weapons and armor can be fully repaired for a quarter of their original price. Depleted toolkits and consumables need outright replacing. Selling: items generally sell for half their listed price, better with a CHA-based check or real rapport with the buyer. title: Magic Items
text: Charged/consumables priced at the tier's casting cost. Permanent items priced at 10–20× the tier's average casting cost — Cantrip/Spark in raw shards, Minor and above in refined shards.

title: Travel
text: GM rolls a d6 for days until a Travel Event (d8 with a relevant wilderness talent or toolkit; −1 on treacherous terrain). The d8 upgrade isn't the only lever. title: Encounter Tables
text: Every "roll on the region's encounter table" reference in this document assumes one exists — build it before the party travels there, not during. A good regional encounter table is 8 entries (roll a d8), mixing genuine danger with texture that isn't combat at all. 4–5 entries of real danger — something that can genuinely hurt the party if handled badly. Build these with Enemy Design Philosophy if nothing existing fits. 2–3 entries of texture, not combat — a sign of danger already passed, a landmark, a fellow traveler, weather worth describing. 1 entry that's genuinely good news — a shortcut, a safe camp, something useful found. Reuse Reaction Check for anything with a mind of its own rather than baking disposition into the table itself. Sharn (urban, dense, House-controlled): d8 Encounter 1 A House Deneith enforcer patrol, checking papers — real if minor legal risk if anything's amiss 2

title: Exploration Procedure
text: A player's own specific, declared action always comes first — "I check under the rug," "I run my hand along the statue's base." These get resolved on their own terms, GM's call on what check applies. The four actions below are only the default behaviors for a Turn when nothing more specific is being declared. Each Turn (10 minutes) while exploring a site, the party takes one of the following, then the GM rolls the Exploration Event check. Move — travel to an adjacent area or room. No check needed. Search — a careful, deliberate look for hidden doors, traps, or overlooked treasure. One roll for the whole party — 2d10 + the highest INT bonus among the searching characters — vs the location's Target (12 by default, shiftable per Scenario Target Modifiers ). Ties up the whole Turn. Listen at a door — a quick check before committing to a room, doesn't use up the Turn's main action. Roll 2d10+

title: Enemy Design Philosophy — Legendary Resistance
text: A true solo boss auto-succeeds its first 3 failed resistance checks per encounter. Without this, sustained control from 2–3 dedicated casters can lock a boss out of acting almost entirely. Controllers Lockdown rate 1 1.0% 2 9.3% 3 22.4% A boss's resist Target is just its Base Target, scaled like everything else — no separate stat needed, unless a specific monster has a resist exception (a Lich's undead mind, a Dragon's magic-soaked hide). Applies only to named threats built with Multi-Action.

title: Enemy Design Philosophy — Scenario Target Modifiers
text: The full Target-shift table lives in Core Resolution , at the top of the document — the same two levers (Target shift, Advantage/Disadvantage) apply everywhere, not just to enemies. Morale's Target 12 is a default, not a fixed value — use that same table to design a specific group's steadiness. A disciplined or fanatical unit (Karrnathi line infantry, Silver Flame zealots) can hold at Target 9 or lower using the +3 row. A green, poorly-paid, or genuinely terrified group (raw conscripts, monsters way out of their depth) can break at Target 15 or higher using the −3 row. Set it once per enemy group at design time, the same way HP or attack bonus gets set — not something rolled fresh each encounter. Previous ← Exploration Next Advancement →

title: Experience & Leveling
text: Level up at XP = 5× current level, resetting to 0 after each level-up — level 2 needs a fresh 5 XP, level 3 a fresh 10, level 4 a fresh 15, and so on up through level 8's fresh 35. Since a single session's highest die can never exceed 8 (the biggest die is a d8), and every threshold past level 2 already exceeds 8, no single session can ever clear more than one level-up — the reset itself prevents skipping ahead. Max level 8.

title: Experience & Leveling — Themed Question Packages
text: XP is awarded via end-of-session questions, each scaled by a die (d4/d6/d8) by scope — highest result is XP for everyone. The five confirmed questions work fine as a generic default, but XP questions are a campaign's actual incentive structure — they tell players what their characters should be doing. Pick a package matching the table's real focus, or mix five questions from different ones. Same mechanic throughout, only the categories change. title: Experience & Leveling — Leveling Procedure, Worked Example
text: After every session, add the highest die result to the party's current-level XP tally. If it now meets or exceeds 5× current level, everyone levels up and the tally resets to 0 — the next threshold is calculated fresh from the new, higher level. Worked Example — Tracking XP Across Sessions Dungeon Delvers package, a level-1 party starting at 0 XP toward a level-2 threshold of 5: Session 1: a modest hoard (treasure, moderate — d6, result 4); a trap dodged cleverly (minor — d4, result 2). Highest: 4. Tally: 0→4. Doesn't clear 5 — stays level 1. Session 2: someone survives Death's Door (major — d8, result 3). Tally: 4→7. Clears 5 — levels up to 2 , tally resets to 0, next threshold is 5×2=10. Session 3: the dungeon's goal is completed (major — d8, result 6). Tally: 0→6. Doesn't clear 10 — stays level 2. Session 4: another trap solved (minor — d4, result 3). Tally: 6→9. Still doesn't clear 1

title: Vertical & Lateral Growth
text: Each level-up: choose Vertical (+1 to one stat — hard capped at +3, no stat can ever exceed +3 under any circumstance. A maxed 3d6 roll alone caps at +2; stacking a same-stat Background bonus on top of a maxed roll can already reach +3 at character creation, before any Vertical growth at all. A stat already at +3 simply isn't a legal target for a further pick — the player picks a different stat instead, same as any other level-up — plus +1 flat Guard , identical for everyone, uncapped) and Lateral (archetype-specific — see Archetypes for the full per-level tables). Nothing is pre-selected; every choice is made fresh at the moment it's earned. Track Cadence What grows Vertical Every other level (2,4,6,8) +1 to one stat, +1 flat Guard Lateral Every level New options, per archetype Second Wound slot unlocks at level 4, third at level 8. title: Aberrant Mark
text: Aberrant Mark — grants a Minor-tier cast attempt with zero shards ever possessed, meaning every use is a genuine Overcast, resolved entirely through the existing Overcast Backlash Pool. No separate mechanic — reuses casting and Overcasting directly.

title: Advantage / Disadvantage
text: Advantage / Disadvantage — roll 3d10 instead of 2d10, keep the best two (Advantage) or worst two (Disadvantage). Disadvantage rolls never crit. Never stacks within a single roll — that roll has one, the other, or neither. Strictly per-roll, not per-character: a PC's own outgoing attack and an enemy's incoming attack against that PC are separate rolls that never interact.

title: Archetype
text: Archetype — the three character chassis: Wayfarer, Agent, Syberist (the latter with four traditions — Shardbound, Flamesworn, Wildspoken, Artificer). Determines resource type, Lateral Advancement track, and Guard bonus.

title: Background
text: Background — race and culture fused into one character-creation choice. Grants a stat bonus, two Talents, and narrative-only gear.

title: Base Target
text: Base Target — the single number an enemy uses for attacking, defending, and resisting Effect spells, before Encounter Level Scaling. Weak 9, Standard 12, Strong 15.

title: Cast Stat
text: Cast Stat — the stat a Syberist uses for spellcasting. Always distinct from Guard Stat and weapon stat — never merged, even when it's a character's defining stat.

title: Contingency
text: Contingency — what Leverage buys: retroactively declaring you already prepared for a specific moment. Cost scales with the size of the ask (1/2/3+ Leverage).

title: Contraption
text: Contraption — an Artificer Syberist's built-ahead device, sealed with a Name-Crafted effect via Quick Rig. Triggered later as a single action by whoever holds it, using their own INT bonus for the roll — not the crafter's.

title: Critical Hit
text: Critical Hit — doubles on the to-hit roll (both counted dice match a success). Deals maximum damage, no damage roll. Advantage can still crit if the kept two dice match; Disadvantage never crits, under any circumstance.

title: Damage Floor
text: Damage Floor — any successful hit deals a minimum of 1 damage, regardless of die result or negative stat bonus. Universal, not specific to any one weapon, spell, or interaction.

title: Day
text: Day — a real-world day, no special game definition. Used for Deprivation's multi-day survival tracking, Wounds' passive recovery, and a few explicit time costs.

title: Death's Door
text: Death's Door — triggered at 0 Guard with no Wound slots remaining. Roll d6: 1–3 dies, 4+ faints and rolls on the Scar Table. A fainted character still dies if not treated within a Turn by another character.

title: Deprivation
text: Deprivation — see Status Effects. Disadvantage on all checks and no Guard recovery from resting a Turn, from failing to gather food/rest during travel.

title: Disengage Check
text: Disengage Check — a DEX check (2d10+DEX vs 12) required to leave a zone containing a live melee hostile. Failure grants them a free attack first.

title: Effect Spell
text: Effect Spell — a spell that isn't an attack (wards, buffs, heals, utility). No caster roll; works automatically on a willing target, resistance check on an unwilling one. Contrast Attack Spell .

title: Encounter / Fight
text: Encounter / Fight — used interchangeably with Scene specifically when the context is combat. "Once per encounter" and "once per scene" draw from the same budget, not two separate pools.

title: Grit
text: Grit — Wayfarer's resource. Starts at 2, +1 at even levels. +1 per Turn of rest (if not Deprived), up to your max. Spent on Grit Maneuvers.

title: Guard
text: Guard — the damage buffer every character has. = 4 + Guard Stat bonus + archetype bonus + armor + shield, floor 1. Restores fully after a Turn of rest.

title: Guard Stat
text: Guard Stat — calculated automatically: your highest-bonus stat, excluding cast stat and the governing stat of every equipped weapon. Stable by default, but recalculates immediately if a mid-combat equipment change (always a full action) alters the exclusions.

title: Initiative
text: Initiative — 2d10 + DEX + weapon modifier − armor penalty, rolled once per fight. Fixed order for the whole encounter.

title: Leverage
text: Leverage — Agent's resource. Starts at 2, +1 per level. Regenerates during downtime via a GM-adjudicated check, not from resting a Turn.

title: Lateral (Advancement track)
text: Lateral (Advancement track) — the archetype-specific options gained every level, no exceptions. Contrast Vertical .

title: Legendary Resistance
text: Legendary Resistance — a true solo boss auto-succeeds its first 3 failed resistance checks per encounter.

title: Milestone
text: Milestone — the encounter-scaling checkpoint, tied to party level (roughly every 2 levels). Drives Encounter Level Scaling for mooks, bosses, and Base Target.

title: Mook
text: Mook — an enemy with no Wound slot — Guard alone determines when it's down. Contrast Named .

title: Multi-Action
text: Multi-Action — extra actions per Round granted to true solo bosses, scaling with Milestones reached.

title: Named
text: Named — an enemy with the full Guard → Wound → Scar chain, same as a PC. Contrast Mook .

title: Overcast Backlash Pool
text: Overcast Backlash Pool — the dice-pool mechanic resolving what happens when a caster attempts a Minor+ tier cast without enough shards.

title: Overcasting
text: Overcasting — attempting a Minor, Moderate, Major, or Mythic cast without enough shards on hand. Never applies to Cantrip or Spark, which have flat, known costs.

title: Quick Rig
text: Quick Rig — an Artificer Syberist's baseline casting method: Name-Craft a spell during downtime, seal it into a Contraption instead of firing it immediately. Takes 1 Turn per Contraption, cannot happen mid-combat.

title: Rattled
text: Rattled — see Status Effects. Disadvantage on your next two rolls, from a Wound Complication or another source.

title: Reeling
text: Reeling — see Status Effects. Disadvantage on your next roll, from a Wound opening or another source.

title: Round
text: Round — one full cycle through the fixed Initiative order, the unit combat is measured in. Not to be confused with Turn below, a completely different, much longer exploration-pacing unit.

title: Scar Table
text: Scar Table — the d10 table rolled when a character faints at Death's Door (result of 4+).

title: Scenario Target Modifier
text: Scenario Target Modifier — the GM's tool for shifting a Target up or down based on circumstance, on the same granular scale used for enemy Base Targets and Leverage regeneration checks.

title: Scene
text: Scene — a bounded dramatic sequence: a fight, a chase, a tense negotiation, a leg of a journey. GM calls when one starts and ends. Broader than combat specifically — see Encounter/Fight for the combat-context synonym.

title: Session
text: Session — one full sitting at the table. The coarsest tracked unit; a single session can contain many scenes. Used for XP questions and anything explicitly limited "per session," a larger budget than "per scene."

title: Shards, Raw (Dust)
text: Shards, Raw (Dust) — loose, unrefined, 5cp each. Powers Cantrip and Spark tier only.

title: Shards, Refined
text: Shards, Refined — cut and processed, 10gp each. Powers Minor tier and above, and permanent magic items.

title: Shock
text: Shock — a monster-specific trait: minimum chip damage on a miss with melee attacks (Light 1, Medium/Heavy 2), gated by the target's armor tier.

title: Skill
text: Skill — an Agent's chosen ability, picked freely at creation and every level-up (Swift, Network, Expertise, Many Pockets).

title: Status Effects
text: Status Effects — the four named temporary states used throughout this document: Reeling, Rattled, Deprived, Surprised. Full table on Combat .

title: Surprised
text: Surprised — see Status Effects. Skip your action entirely for Round 1 of a fight; clears automatically after.

title: Talent
text: Talent — a Background-granted ability that gives Advantage on a narrow, named category of checks.

title: Target
text: Target — the number a 2d10+stat roll must meet or beat to succeed. Standard 12; shifted by tier or Scenario Target Modifier.

title: Tier (magic)
text: Tier (magic) — Cantrip, Spark, Minor, Moderate, Major, Mythic — the six potency levels of a cast, each with its own shard cost and damage output.

title: Turn
text: Turn — a 10-minute unit of exploration/downtime pacing (OSE/B-X convention) — wandering monster checks, resource use, and resting are all measured in Turns. This document does not use "Turn" for an individual's action in combat — that's covered entirely by Round above. There's also no formal "short rest / long rest" mechanic here — Guard restores after a Turn of rest (10 minutes), and Wounds close after a full day's rest, both already real units this system tracks natively.

title: Vertical (Advancement track)
text: Vertical (Advancement track) — the universal stat/Guard growth every archetype shares, every other level (2, 4, 6, 8). Contrast Lateral .

title: Weapon Stat
text: Weapon Stat — the stat (STR or DEX) governing a weapon's attack and damage. Always distinct from cast stat, chosen independently even by a caster who also carries a weapon.

title: Wound
text: Wound — opens when damage overflows a character's Guard and a slot is available. Reduces max Guard by 2; current Guard refills to the new max. Triggers Reeling and a Wound Complication.

title: Wound Complication
text: Wound Complication — the d6 side-effect table rolled when a Wound opens.

title: Zone
text: Zone — the abstracted positioning unit: Melee, Near, Far. Read relative to each character individually, not a shared line — see Zones & Range . Move covers 0–1 zone per turn.
